errors.detail: Para 5, Mr. MALIK (Lebanon) 'had little to add to his previous statements', is a separate turn, but the segment folds it into Mendez's para 4 speech.
The underlined vote line ('The motion was adopted by 10 votes to none, with 1 abstention') sits inside Mendez's speech segment. It should be its own vote segment.
Ingles segment ends with Rizk's first reply ('Replying to a question by Mr. JUVIGNY (France) and a comment by Mr. GHORBAL (Egypt), Mr. RIZK (Lebanon) said...'), a separate turn on the page.
Rizk's speech segment ends with the underlined procedural line 'The Lebanese motion was put to the vote.', which should be a vote segment of its own, not speech text.
Tyabji segment (pp. 6-7) ends with the heading 'CLAUSES RELATING TO THE ADMISSIBILITY AND NON-ADMISSIBILITY OF RESERVATIONS (E/CN.4/677...)' from page 7; it should be its own heading segment.
YU's segment, which runs from the previous page, ends with this page's running header 'E/C:..4/9R.251' and some garbled text. The scan shows the header 'E/CN.4/SR.251 page 31' at the top of the page.
Santa Cruz's turn ends on this page after 'the Secretariat.' The segment then runs on into the turn of Mr. Morozov (USSR), which starts on the next page, so it holds two speakers.

Page ends with a second turn by Mrs. ROOSEVELT (United States of America) 'thought that the Commission should take a decision on the matter now'. The Morozov segment runs through it, ending with her text on page 6 ('exclude the possibility...').
The Chairman's reply ends 'the submission was in order.' on the page. Segment 0007 stops at 'the'; the closing words 'submission was in order.' are at the end of the masthead segment 0003.
Morozov's first speech ends 'both articles together.' Segment 0008 stops at 'both articles.'; the last word 'together.' opens procedural segment 0005.
Segment 0005 opens with the running symbol 'E/CN.4/SR: 325' and the catchword '/There was', mixed into the agenda-item text.

The underlined subheading 'Chilean delegation's amendment to article 18' is not its own heading segment. It sits at the end of the procedural agenda segment 0005, while 'Articles 15 and 16' does get its own heading.
The agenda item is split. Its tail 'E/CN.4/L.202, E/CN.4/L.203) (continued)' is in masthead segment 0003, and the rest is in segment 0005, in jumbled order.

Off this page, not counted as an error here: the chair's turn ends on p12, where he calls on the Sub-Commission chairman, yet the segment runs to p18. It probably absorbs later speakers' turns on pp13-18.

Para 32 on the page ends with the closing lines 'législatives ou autres qui leur portent atteinte...' or possibly '...de mesures législatives ou administratives qui leur portent atteinte...'. The segment (pages 4-4) stops at '...de mesures', so those lines are in no segment.
Para 26 'Miss FUJITA (Japan)' starts a new turn on this page (paras 26-31), but her speech is inside the Hoare (United Kingdom) segment, which ends with her para 31 text.

Footnote 1 at the foot of the left column ('Official Records of the Economic and Social Council, Twenty-second Session, Supplement No. 8, annex II, resolution II A') is appended to the end of Petrzelka's speech text.
Valenzuela's segment ends with '82.', the paragraph number of Rochefort's turn; segment 0040 opens 'Mr. ROCHEFORT' without its number. Turn split and speakers are otherwise right.

Chair segment (para 32) also holds the first two italic vote results (para 1: 88-0-3; para 2: 91-0-1). Only the third amendment and article 36 votes are in the vote segment 0024, so the vote block is split.
The heading 'Conclusion of the Committee's work' at the top of page 5 is appended to the vote segment from page 4 instead of being its own heading segment.

Chair's para 2 segment also holds the vote line and the whole AGENDA ITEM 43 heading (Draft International Covenants... PROPOSALS FOR ADDITIONAL SUBSTANTIVE ARTICLES (concluded)), which should be a separate heading segment.
Bouquin's speech carries the page-foot symbol 'A/C.3/S8R.1202' between 'took up the' and 'draft International Covenants' across the page break.

On the image, 'The CHAIRMAN stated that a new proposal regarding torture...' (with the UK text and 'She pointed out...') starts a new turn. The segment is still Wilson's and ends with the Chairman's words.

Agenda heading 'CONTINUATION OF CONSIDERATION OF DRAFT INTERNATIONAL DECLARATION ON HUMAN RIGHTS (document E/CN.4/95)' above 'Article 3' is in no segment listed for this page. The NGO attendance list is also absent, which may be intentional masthead.
Pavlov's opening runs 'He supported the right of Page 10 ~ w...': the running header of the next page ('Page 10') is still in the speech text where it crosses the page break.
Mrs. VERWEY-JONKER (Netherlands) requesting a roll-call vote is a separate turn on the page, but it sits at the end of the Corbet (United Kingdom) segment.

Pleic's speech ends with the French quotation 'Les enfants nés hors du mariage sont les égaux en droit des enfants nés dans le mariage...'. The segment stops at 'hors du', so the rest of the quotation looks lost.
The page opens with a new turn, 'The CHAIRMAN pointed out that Mr. BORISOV had asked...'. The segment's ending shows this Chairman turn joined to Daniels' speech from page 3.
At the foot of the page, the turn 'The CHAIRMAN pointed out that, as the Sub-Commission was...' begins after Nisot's short request. The segment's opening shows it joined to Nisot's speech.

Image shows Mr. HUMPHREY (Secretariat) starting a new turn after Mrs. Popova's proposal; the segment's ending holds Humphrey's 'thought that the Commission might make recommendations...' inside Popova's speech.
The page prints 'Mr. KHOMUSSKO (Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic)' as the speaker. The segment has speaker null, though its delegation is right and the turn is split correctly.
Footnote 1 ('See Annex 17, page 296') belongs to the Seventieth Meeting's heading 35 (document E/330), lower on the page. That is another meeting, but this footnote sits in E/PV.69.

Footnote 2 belongs to the 70th meeting's President's statement on genocide, not E/PV.69. Its text is also cut short: it stops at 'General Assembly', and 'during the second part of its first session, resolution 96 (I), page 188' is missing.
The chair segment also holds the separate narrative paragraph 'There followed some discussion on the agenda and the programme of future work', which is not the President speaking.

The President's opening speech ('The first item on the agenda is the General Committee's report...' through 'Cuban representative's attention to this point') is not its own chair segment. It sits inside the procedural masthead/contents segment.

The agenda heading '18. Supplementary List of Items for Inclusion in the Agenda... Report of the General Committee' is printed on its own but is not a separate heading segment. It is merged into the procedural segment with the masthead, contents and the President's speech.
The President's turn 'I would mention that we have discussed the position with the Chairman of the Sixth Committee...' starts on this page but is inside Perez Cisneros's segment.
Perez Cisneros's second turn ('The Cuban delegation accepts that interpretation') comes after the President's reply but is not split off. It stays in the same segment as his first question.

The President's turn at the foot of the column ('The PRESIDENT (Translation from the French): I thank the Cuban representative... paragraph 4 (a) is adopted') is inside the Cuban segment; the segment's ending shows it.
Opening carries French-column words 'voudrions savoir 4 quelle commission on envisage' (from Pérez Cisneros's French A/163 turn) spliced inside the English 'To an Assembly like ours, com-posed of'.
Valenzuela (Chile) starts a turn under the 'Paragraphs 5 to 7' heading. His objection ('characterized as charters of the right to take life...') sits inside a vote segment with no speaker.
The heading 'Paragraphs 5 to 7' at the top of the page has no segment of its own. It seems to be merged, garbled, into the vote segment carried over from page 14.
The CHAIRMAN's turn ('After an exchange of views, the CHAIRMAN proposed... arbitrarily deprived of his life') is inside Morozov's segment.
The underlined decision 'Paragraphs 5 to 7, with the Chilean-United Kingdom and Uruguayan amendments... were adopted' should be its own vote segment. It sits at the end of Morozov's speech.
The ending 'PAs pripn' looks like the garbled catchword '/Paragraphs 8 and 9' at the foot of the page.
Ending of the Santa Cruz speech from page 6 carries this page's running symbol 'eee B/CN.4/5R. 308' (E/CN.4/SR.308 header).
Ending carries debris 'es ae Ning deen 308', apparently the catchword and the next page's E/CN.4/SR.308 header.
The underlined vote result ('The Commission refused to receive the Polish amendment by 8 votes to 3, with 6 abstentions') is in the chair segment, not a separate vote segment.
Page has Mr. KAECKENBEECK (Belgium) then 'Mr. MELOVSKI (Yugoslavia) said he had studied the Chilean proposal'; the segment runs on to the Yugoslav speech, so both turns are in one Belgium segment.
Ending contains 'page & Se', the garbled page-8 running header, before 'The Yugoslav delegation would therefore vote...'.

Mrs. MEHTA (India) starts her own turn after the Chairman's ruling ('pointed out the obvious difficulties...'), but the chair segment runs on through her speech and ends with her closing words 'be justiciable rights to be included in the Covenant'.
Birecki's speech ends on page 6, but its ending carries page 7's running symbol 'E/CN.4/SR.4 ›c' (header E/CN.4/SR.436), which also stretches its pages to 5-7.
The underlined decision 'Document E/CN.4/L.366/Add.12 was adopted, subject to those amendments.' sits inside Morozov's speech. It should be its own vote/decision segment.
The underlined heading 'Document E/CN.4/L.366/Add.13' runs into the end of Morozov's speech ('Document E/CN /L. 366/Add a3'). It should be a separate heading segment.

Para 27, 'Mr. KYROU (Greece) invited the representative of the Secretary-General...', starts on this page. It has no segment of its own: Cassin's segment (para 25, from p. 8) ends with Kyrou's text. The segment also runs over the Danish speaker's continuation and the Commission's decision line.
Whitlam's segment ending carries 'page 1%', which is the garbled running header 'page 12' from the top of this page (below E/CN.4/SR.370), left in the speech text.

Pazhwak's segment ends with '88. In reply to a question from the CHAIRMAN,', the opening of Lopez Villamil's turn (para 88); segment 0029 starts at 'Mr. LOPEZ VILLAMIL'. Speakers are right, but the boundary is misplaced.

Baroody's segment ends with '90. In reply to a question from the CHAIRMAN,', the opening of Yoacham's turn (para 90); segment 0031 starts at 'Mr. YOACHAM'. Speakers are right, but the boundary is misplaced.

The italic decision line 'There being no objection, the motion was adopted.' is attached to the end of Mani's speech. The italic suspension line that follows it is its own procedural segment (0004), so the two are handled differently.
Image prints para 6 as 'Mr. BRAÑA (Cuba)'. The segment's own opening also reads BRANA, but its speaker field says CORTINA, a different name.
De Arenas speech ending carries the masthead text 'THIRD COMMITTEE 866th MEETING ... 29 October 1958, at 10.55 a.m NEW YORK' after 'paragraph by paragraph'.

The page opens with a new labelled turn: '158. The PRESIDENT: We shall first take up draft resolution A...'. Segment 0057 (para 157, pp. 14-15) runs through it and on to the vote A abstentions, so 158 has no segment of its own.
Vote segment for draft resolution B also holds '160. The PRESIDENT: I shall now call on representatives who wish to explain their votes', which is a separate chair turn.
The page prints '161. Mr. Quarles van UFFORD (Netherlands)', but the segment's speaker is null; only the delegation is filled in.

Footnote 8 at the foot of the left column ('The delegation of Argentina subsequently informed the Secretariat...') sits in the chair segment's ending, before 'Against: South Africa, Abstaining: Portugal'.
Sahai speech ends with 'E/3437 and Add.1; E/CN.4/820 and Add.1 and 2,', the second line of footnote 4. Footnote segment 0009 is cut off at 'doc.'.
Footnote 2/ on the image ends 'circulated as document A/C.3/L.1361.'; the segment stops at 'circulated as', so the second line naming the document is in no segment.

Image shows a new turn, Mr. STEPANENKO (Byelorussian SSR), starting mid-page. The Pavlov segment's ending holds Stepanenko's text ('representative from arriving in time... beyond their control'), so his turn is not a separate segment.
The page has a separate turn after Roy: 'The CHAIRMAN called for a vote on Miss MONROE'S amendment...' (Article 13 text). The segment puts it inside Roy's (Haiti) speech.

The vote segment 'adopted by 6 votes to 5' also holds the CHAIRMAN's next turn, where he puts the new Article 13 as a whole to the vote, and the 8-2-1 vote after it. The chair's turn should be its own segment.

Prof. CASSIN's turn ('remarked that the question of compensation...responsibility of arresting officers') starts mid-paragraph after Harry's speech but sits inside Harry's (Australia) segment; the ending shows Cassin's text.
Prof. KORETSKY (USSR) turn ('although reserving his right... condemn slavery in general') starts after Wilson's but is inside Wilson's (United Kingdom) segment; the ending is Koretsky's text.
Page has a separate turn 'Mr. TEPLIAKOV (USSR) moved that the meeting should be adjourned...' after Cassin's speech; the segment runs Cassin's text on into Tepliakov's motion.

The 'DECISION: The ruling of the Chair was sustained by six votes to two' line is folded into Tepliakov's speech rather than a separate vote segment; likewise the adjournment DECISION sits at the end of 0017.

Cassin's speech under Article 9 ('Pointing out a slight discrepancy... Mr. CASSIN (France) requested...') is marked as a vote; it should be a speech. The vote text 'It was so decided' from the next page is joined to it.
The page names Mr. CASSIN (France) as the speaker, but the segment has speaker and delegation null because the name falls in the middle of the opening sentence.
The heading 'ARTICLES 4a, 5, 6 AND 6a' is inside the vote segment, between the Article 4 vote and the vote on articles 4a-6a. It should be its own heading segment.

Segment ends with 'as to marriage par equal matrimonial rights.', a fragment of the French column's Danish-proposal paragraph ('equal rights as to marriage par equal matrimonial rights'), not of the English text.

The chair segment also holds the next turn, 'In reply to a question by Mr. PAVLOV (USSR) the representative of the UNITED KINGDOM said...'. That turn runs down to 'the judiciary was assured' and should be its own speech, for the United Kingdom.

'Mr. HEYWOOD (Australia), s...' starts at the foot of page 5, but no segment begins there. The chair segment runs on to page 6 and ends on what seems to be Heywood's text about 'respective jurisdiction'.

The page has two English footnotes: 1 (E/CN.4/21, annex F, article 36) and 2 (See E/CN.4/95, annex A, article 31). The footnote segment's opening and ending both give only footnote 1, so footnote 2 seems to be in no segment.
The page prints the speaker as 'Mr. SANTA CRUZ (Chile)', and the segment's text itself says 'Mr. Santa Cnuz'. The speaker field reads FERNANDEZ, a different name.
Page prints 'Mr. KHOMUSSKO (Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic)'; the segment has the right delegation but speaker is null (OCR 'Kuonvssxo' not resolved to a name).
Page prints 'Mr. VAN KLEFFENS (Netherlands) pointed out...' and the segment's own opening says van Kleffens, but the speaker field is VAN ROIJEN, a different person.

The opening has footnote text ('1See Resolutions adopted by the General Assembly during the second part of its first sessi...') spliced into Chang's speech. It comes from the previous page's footnote.
